answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may post bids or vote, then randomly sample accounts for tasks and weight their influence by stake at risk rather than by account count. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply the locked value or voting weight; matching honest influence means acquiring and immobilizing more stake, which can be forfeited if sampled agents expose coordinated fraud. A walnut-sized forge may look cheap, but scaling it against a gale of independent checks gets costly.
